Register of gambling businesses

Search by business name, trading name, domain name or account number

Full register

View and filter the full gambling business register

2,631 records

Download the register

Register data is available in Excel, CSV and as a Zip file with all datasets in this register.

About the data

Last updated: 05 November 2026

Domain names and trading names are provided by the gambling business. The Gambling Commission cannot guarantee the accuracy of information provided by third parties.

The fields in this register

Field Description
Account number The unique reference number of the business
Account name The legal name of the gambling business
Head office address The current recorded head office for this business, please note that the full address may not show due to requests made by the business
Licence status The status of the licence


Active - Licence is active and up to date
Expired - Indicates that a licensee has not applied to the Commission for a new operating licence after the current licence reaches its end date
Forfeited - Indicates that a court has ordered the licence to no longer have affect
Lapsed - As a result of the business being liquidated, sequestrated or declared bankrupt; or a licensee is unable to carry out the licensed activities by reason of mental or physical incapacity
Pending - New licence has been applied for or is being varied and not yet active
Revoked - Licence revoked as a result of regulatory action or breach of licence conditions
Revoked (Non payment of fee) - Licence revoked as a result of annual fee not being paid
Surrendered - Licence has been given up by the business as it is no longer required
Suspended - Licence has been suspended by the Gambling Commission pending investigation

Activity from The date the business was most recently granted a licence to operate this product
Activity until The date the business stopped operating this product
Trading name count The number of trading names declared by the business to the Gambling Commission
Domain name count The number of domain names declared by the business to the Gambling Commission
Premises count The number of premises for the business known to the Gambling Commission
Trading name status The status of the trading name, this can be "Active" or "Inactive"
Domain name status The status of the domain name, this can be "Active", "Inactive" or "White label"
Regulatory actions Sanctions and/or settlements imposed by the Gambling Commission as a result of regulatory action or investigation.

29 October 2026
MGA Concludes Consultation on Proposed Updates to Recognition Notice Framework

The Malta Gaming Authority has completed its review of feedback submitted during the targeted consultation on proposed updates to the Recognition Notice (RN) Framework and thanks all stakeholders who participated and shared their views.

The consultation offered a valuable opportunity to consider the proposed approach and its practical application. The feedback received informed a number of refinements to ensure that the revised approach remains proportionate, risk-based and practical for RN holders.

A Feedback Statement summarising the feedback received, the Authority’s position and the way forward has been circulated to RN holders and their representatives. The Authority will share further information on the practical application of specific requirements in due course.
The Authority has amended paragraph 4 of the Recognition Notice with effect from 1 December 2026 to require licensees to submit amended control system documentation for review.

26 October 2026
‘Make It In Malta’ Heads to SiGMA World 2026 to Showcase Malta’s Gaming Ecosystem

Following its debut earlier this year, the Make It In Malta initiative will continue its international outreach at SiGMA World 2026, taking place in Rome from 3 to 5 November.

Having established a presence at ICE Barcelona and SBC Summit Lisbon, the initiative now heads to Rome for its third major international exhibition of the year.

Through a shared exhibition stand under the Make It In Malta banner, the Malta Gaming Authority will once again join forces with GamingMalta, Identità, Malta Enterprise and Bank of Valletta to showcase Malta’s gaming ecosystem.

The initiative was launched to present a broader picture of what Malta offers gaming businesses beyond regulation alone. By bringing together entities spanning regulation, business and investment support, visa and identity services, and banking, Make It In Malta highlights the comprehensive support available to gaming businesses at every stage of their journey, from establishing a presence in Malta to supporting their ongoing operations and growth.

SiGMA World brings together gaming industry stakeholders from around the world, offering an opportunity for the Maltese delegation to engage directly with operators, suppliers, investors and service providers while highlighting Malta’s position as a leading gaming jurisdiction. The event is expected to attract more than 30,000 delegates and over 1,200 sponsors and exhibitors, creating a unique environment for meaningful connections and industry engagement on a global scale.

Throughout the event, representatives from the participating organisations will engage with industry stakeholders, exchange insights on emerging developments, and showcase the different components of Malta’s gaming ecosystem.

The Make It In Malta stand will be located at H3-3087.

Meetings with the MGA or any of the participating entities may be booked here.

23 October 2026
MGA and MCCAA sign Memorandum of Understanding to enhance cooperation on player protection

The Malta Gaming Authority (MGA) and the Malta Competition and Consumer Affairs Authority (MCCAA) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at strengthening cooperation on matters relating to consumer affairs and player protection within the gaming sector.

Through the MoU, the MGA and MCCAA will take a more coordinated approach to addressing consumer concerns, complaints and dispute-related matters that intersect their respective remits. The agreement establishes a formal framework for collaboration, communication and the exchange of relevant information, in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements. By clarifying channels for cooperation, the MoU will help both Authorities identify the appropriate course of action, provide clearer guidance and support better outcomes for consumers and players.

The agreement strengthens cooperation between the MGA and MCCAA in this area, helping ensure that consumers are directed to the appropriate authority and receive the necessary support.

Commenting on the signing of the MoU, MGA Chief Executive Officer Charles Mizzi said: “Effective player protection requires more than strong regulatory frameworks. It also depends on authorities working together, sharing expertise and ensuring that consumers do not fall through the gaps between their respective remits. This agreement strengthens our ability to do just that, reinforcing our commitment to a regulatory environment where player interests remain firmly at the forefront.”

Commenting on the MoU, MCCAA Executive Chairperson Carmen Ciantar remarked: “The protection of consumers remains at the heart of our work. This agreement formalises an already constructive relationship between the MCCAA and the MGA and provides a clear framework for cooperation that will help ensure that consumer concerns arising within the gaming sector are addressed efficiently and effectively.”

The signing of this MoU marks an important step in strengthening cooperation between the MGA and MCCAA and reinforces their shared commitment to safeguarding the interests of consumers and players.

MCCAA Executive Chairperson Carmen Ciantar and MGA CEO Charles Mizzi (right) sign an MoU.

Our public statements make reference to breaches of the Licence Conditions and Codes of Practice (LCCP) requirements which were in effect at the time of the breach. In some cases, the requirements have since been updated.

Operators are expected to consider the issues outlined below and review their own practices to identify and implement improvements in respect of the management of customers’ accounts.

Introduction

Licensed gambling operators have a legal duty to ensure that their gambling facilities are provided in compliance with the Gambling Act 2005 (opens in new tab)(the Act), the conditions of their licence and in accordance with the licensing objectives, which are to:

prevent gambling from being a source of crime or disorder, being associated with crime or disorder or being used to support crime
ensure that gambling is conducted in a fair, safe and open way
protect children and other vulnerable people from being harmed or exploited by gambling.

Operators are expected to consider the issues outlined below and, if applicable to their licence, review their own practices to identify and implement improvements.

Stakelogic BV Executive Summary

An investigation was commenced, outside of a section 116 licence review, following the submission of a Key Event by Stakelogic BV (“the Licensee”). The Licensee reported to the Commission that one of the online slots games it offered to GB consumers was not compliant with a Responsible Product Design Remote Technical Standard (RTS) requiring there to be a minimum of 2.5 seconds from the time a game is started until the next game cycle can be commenced. The Licensee had corrected the fault by the time it had informed the Commission.

The Commission requested further information from the Licensee to ascertain the scope of the failing and the cause.

The investigation found that:

the Licensee failed to comply with Licence Condition (LC) 2.3.1 – specifically RTS requirement 14D between 31 October 20211 and 30 October 20252
a further 15 games were not compliant with RTS requirement 14D, however by smaller margins. The Licensee made the decision to disable all games available to the GB market as soon as the scope of the issues became clear
the errors arose due to the Licensee’s practice of conducting timing checks with a manual stopwatch. The practice of utilising a stopwatch to measure small time intervals is open to significant inaccuracy
the internal processes, procedures and controls fell short of the standards reasonably expected of licensees, particularly relating to quality assurance testing and internal incident management.

Based on the remedial action taken by the Licensee and in line with our Statement of Principles for Licensing and regulation, the Licensee will make a total payment in lieu of a financial penalty of £122,835.

Stakelogic BV Findings

Licence Condition 2.3.1 states:

“Licensees must comply with the Commission’s technical standards and with requirements set by the Commission relating to the timing and procedures for testing.”

The Commission’s RTS sets out the remote gambling and software technical standards under section 89 and section 97 of the Act.

Responsible Product Design RTS requirement 14D states:

“It must be a minimum of 2.5 seconds from the time a game is started until the next game cycle can be commenced. It must always be necessary to release and then depress the 'start button’ or take equivalent action to commence a game cycle.”

The Licensee confirmed that from 28 May 2025 to 30 May 2025, it made available to GB consumers through sites operated by several licensed operators, a game which did not comply with the requirements of 14D of the RTS.

Tiger Temple 88 operated with 1.97 seconds between when the game was started and the next game cycle was commenced; thereby breaching the 2.5 seconds requirement. The error was found to be the result of ineffective manual testing.

Following enquiries made by the Commission, the Licensee conducted re-testing of its entire portfolio of games offered to the GB market. This testing identified a further 15 games which were non-compliant with the requirements of 14D of the RTS.

The non-compliant games were made available to GB consumers during various periods between 31 October 2021 and 30 October 2025, with a range of between 0.001 seconds to 0.675 seconds below the minimum stated in the RTS. The majority of these games operated with a less significant timing error, when compared to the Tiger Temple 88 game. Many of the games were 42 milliseconds or below the cycle requirements. Corrective action was taken and all games were removed from the GB market while the matter was being addressed.

The Licensee accepted its processes fell short of the requirements and resulted in the failure to comply with LC 2.3.1. The Licensee has committed to making significant changes to its quality assurance testing, incident management processes, and to its wider regulatory compliance framework.

Stakelogic BV Regulatory settlement

This regulatory settlement consists of:

a payment in lieu of a financial penalty of £122,835 (which will be directed to the consolidated fund)
agreement to the publication of a statement of facts in relation to this case
payment towards the Commission’s costs of investigating the case.

In considering an appropriate resolution to this investigation, the Commission has had regard to the following aggravating and mitigating factors:

Aggravating factors
the Licensee’s decision not to suspend the Tiger Temple game upon first discovering it was non-compliant. The issue was discovered on 28 May 2025 but remained live until 30 May 2025, when a fix was deployed. If immediate action had been taken this would have minimised impact of the issue
the timeliness of the decision to review all GB products. This action was not taken immediately when the Tiger Temple non compliant game was identified, demonstrating that the incident was managed through a limited and insufficient incident management process. As the Tiger Temple issue was the result of the use of a manual timer, it should have immediately raised concerns that this may be a wider issue if the same methodology had been used across other games
the full scope of the issue was only determined when the Licensee began a much wider review as a result of Commission enquiries.
Mitigating factors
the Licensee disabled all of the games available to the GB market upon understanding the scope of the issue
the Licensee fully co-operated with the Commission’s investigation, worked openly and collaboratively with the Commission throughout, and provided information by agreed deadlines
the Licensee accepted the failings at an appropriately early stage in the investigation.
Good practice

RTS 14D was introduced on 31 October 2021, specifically to target the risks associated with intensity of gameplay. The requirement was introduced because research showed that fast game cycle speed is associated with increased risks to the consumer.

Gambling operators should take account of the failings identified in this investigation to support wider industry learning. Operators should review their own arrangements and take remedial action where necessary, including consideration of the following:

RTS compliance - are you fully compliant with the relevant RTS requirements?
incident management - do you have effective incident management processes in place to ensure issues are identified, escalated and addressed in a timely manner?
measurement of spins - what methodology is used to measure spins, and how is accuracy assured?
testing and assurance - are testing arrangements sufficiently robust, and are appropriate checks undertaken on a regular basis?
Footnotes

1 Date RTS 14D requirement was introduced

2 Date all GB games were disabled

News

News, speeches and announcements from the Gambling Commission.

Featured
New survey data to help tackle illegal gambling and protect consumers

Fresh estimates on the extent of consumer engagement with illegal gambling websites have been published today (5 November) by the Gambling Commission as part of its drive to build better evidence and disrupt illegal markets.

5 November 2026

Enforcement

Three sentenced for General Election betting offences

Three people have been sentenced for offences of cheating relating to bets placed on the date of the 2024 General Election.

23 October 2026

Speeches

IAGR 2026 Conference keynote - Sarah Gardner speech

This speech was delivered by Acting Chief Executive Sarah Gardner at the International Association of Gaming Regulators (IAGR) Conference on 20 October 2026.

21 October 2026

Enforcement

L & L Europe pays £900,000 for failures including withdrawal delays

An online gambling business is to pay £900,000 for regulatory failures, including unnecessarily delaying consumer withdrawals.

21 October 2026

Enforcement

Land-based casino operators to pay £5m for regulatory failures

Three nation-wide casino operators are to pay £5 million after a Gambling Commission investigation revealed anti-money laundering and social responsibility failures.

7 October 2026

Enforcement

Two men sentenced after operating an illegal gambling den

Two men have been given suspended prison sentences for possessing and transferring criminal funds obtained through the running of illegal poker games in Cardiff.

5 October 2026

Speeches

Allwyn Participant Protection Conference - Sarah Gardner speech

This speech was delivered by Acting Chief Executive Sarah Gardner at the Allwyn Participant Protection Conference on Thursday 1 October 2026. Please note: This is the speech as drafted and may slightly differ from the delivered version.

2 October 2026

Industry

New machine rules to support consumers and operators to reduce harm

New standards to make gaming machines fairer and safer for consumers are to be introduced.

30 September 2026

Enforcement

Four arrests and £20,000 seized in illegal gambling raids

The Gambling Commission and Manchester City Council’s Licensing Team supported Greater Manchester Police during raids on four properties this week.

23 September 2026

Enforcement

Suspension of licence – Targetlocal Ltd

The Gambling Commission has suspended the combined remote operating licence of Targetlocal Ltd which trades as Ken Howell’s Sports Betting and runs kenhowells.com.

21 September 2026

Industry

Commission releases gambling industry statistics for 2025 to 2026

The Gambling Commission has today published its Industry Statistics annual report for the financial year April 2025 to March 2026.

17 September 2026

Enforcement

Two more admit General Election betting offences

Today, 10 September, Anthony Lee pleaded guilty to two offences of cheating, contrary to section 42(1)(a) and section 42(1)(b) of the Gambling Act 2005.

10 September 2026

Corporate

Ruth Evans appointed new Chair of the Gambling Commission

The Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) has today announced the appointment of the new Chair of the Gambling Commission.

7 September 2026

Enforcement

Suspension of licences – BresBet Ltd and Bet St George Ltd

The Gambling Commission has suspended the operating licence of BresBet Ltd which runs bresbet.com and Bet St George Ltd which operates betstgeorge.com.

28 August 2026

Enforcement

QuinnBet (Gibraltar) Limited to pay £609,104 for regulatory failures

An online gambling business is to pay £609,104 after a Commission investigation revealed anti-money laundering and social responsibility failures.

20 August 2026

Enforcement

Holland Park Leisure Limited fined £150,000

An Adult Gaming Centre operator is to pay a £150,000 fine for failing to comply with a self-exclusion requirement designed to reduce gambling harm.

18 August 2026

Enforcement

Commission supports police action targeting illegal gambling activity

The Gambling Commission has supported South Yorkshire Police in a coordinated operation targeting illegal gambling and suspected organised criminal activity in Sheffield and Doncaster.

10 August 2026

National Lottery

Court of Appeal refuses TNLC permission to appeal

The Court of Appeal has refused The New Lottery Company Limited (TNLC) and Northern & Shell PLC’s application to appeal part of the High Court decision from April 2026 which had dismissed all claims against the Gambling Commission.

30 July 2026

Enforcement

Illegal casino arrests

Two people have been arrested as part of an investigation into an illegal casino in Bristol.

29 July 2026

Corporate

Sarah Fox to join the Gambling Commission

A senior leader from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) is to join the Gambling Commission’s Executive Team.

29 July 2026
